decisions.evidence: Proof 2.1 omits the explicit reverse-direction assumption that (r+J)(s+J)=rs+J is independent of representatives. Conversely immediately supplies the intended assumption. With it, for every r in R and j in J, j+J=0+J forces rj+J=0+J and jr+J=0+J, hence rj,jr in J by the cited coset criterion. The additive-subgroup hypothesis supplies the remaining ideal axioms. Step 1.1 separately proves ideal implies well-defined multiplication; thm-quotient-ring-laws F5 usage in the polynomial example needs only that direction. The theorem is true, including J=0, J=R and the zero ring. This is nonfatal recoverable proof polish; published source remains read-only and owner maintenance is pending.
